variants.name: tool as built
variants.why: control: the layered lock sweeps starter (H36) on the current baseline; its reader check is still pending, and every other variant is read against it and against the baseline (gap rows 1 and 2)
variants.head: head-2578

variants.name: uneven lock lengths
variants.why: critic issue 1 and R03.4: the even overlap reads as a pine branch; keep ten primaries per side but vary lengths .80 to 1.05 of the table so the edge is a run of long and short points, wing tips held at .98 so R03.1 stays at the sheet span; H36 only (about 1 minute)
variants.head: head-2588

variants.name: primaries lead, secondaries tuck
variants.why: R03.4 and R03.7 (no flat leaf plane): wider over-layer primaries (1.15) with a deeper stagger (.03) and short under-layer secondaries (.80) so the visible edge is nine big points and the secondaries only fill between them; H36 only
variants.head: head-2587

variants.name: wing-end wedge on the character right
variants.why: critic issue 3 and R03.3: the image-left wing end is a rounded lobe with its tops only .01 to .02 above the crown; raise and sharpen RP4 to RP6 (tip up and out, narrower taper) toward the sheet's up-flared point while staying inside the envelope; H36 only
variants.head: head-2589

variants.name: soft wide unions
variants.why: critic issue 2 and R03.7 (no crinkled rim): the serrated seams come from voxel junctions, so widen the unions instead of the pale material: root blend .007, root band .05, seam blur 5, tuft blends and cup fillet up, section .p 2.1; H36 only
variants.head: head-2591

variants.name: deep outward cup
variants.why: gap rank 2 and R04.5 (profile cavity): the front slabs fill the profile window and no pale cup shows from the side; cup opens 48 degrees outward (35 now), floor to .044 deep, tuft stands .028 off the floor so the pale blades read from the side; H36 only
variants.head: head-2592

variants.name: wings swept back in plan
variants.why: R04 issue 1 (profile): the outer wing sits as a straight vertical band; sweep the outer wing tips of both sides back from df .02 to .04 as the R04 depth plan asks, so the profile reads as a curved shell around a cavity; outline in front view is unchanged because only df moves; H36 only

variants.name: fuller pale tuft
variants.why: R03.7 and R03.5: pale tuft must cover at least half of each cup and read as fur; wider and thicker tuft blades (width .9, thick 1.5), wider pale tolerance (.006) and a deeper blend so more of the cup is pale; H36 only
variants.head: head-2594

variants.name: rear dome soft valley
variants.why: R04 issue 2 and R04.7: the continuous crease ledge outlines the smooth dome from behind, with a bead at the top centre; widen the skin blend .006 to .012, clump blend .005, dome blur 10 and cut smoothing 4 in H34 (about 2 minutes with the steps after it); R03 untouched
variants.head: head-2598

variants.name: rear crown tuft lowered
variants.why: R04 issue 3 and R03.3: the C tuft spikes rise above the front fan and flatten the front V tilt; table copy with the six C tips .010 lower (y), everything else equal; H34 only
variants.head: head-2601

variants.name: rear crown tuft dropped
variants.why: R04 issue 3, a stronger test than lowering: drop the C row entirely (rows K,I,M,T,E) so nothing stands on the crown and the V tilt is the fan's own; H34 only
variants.head: head-2605

variants.name: profile pair: deep cup and swept wings
variants.why: R04.5 and audit rank 2 (ear in profile) need both the cup to open sideways and the wing shell to curve back; the two profile ideas together on H36 only, to see whether they add or fight (R03.1 and the front outline must hold)

variants.name: combined front: uneven, wedge, soft, cup
variants.why: the four independent front ideas that do not fight each other (uneven lengths, right wing wedge, soft unions, deeper cup) together, with the rear dome softened and the crown tuft lowered, as the best single candidate for both regions; edits H34 and H36, one extra minute
variants.head: head-2609

variants.name: sweep H36 tuft.standoff=0.012
variants.why: the tool's strongest lever for how separate and proud the pale blades read (.012 flush leaf, .03 wing-like); the default .02 is the least sure setting and quick previews cannot rank it, so test both ends
variants.head: head-2610
